microcards.mastery_tooltip_sw: Synaptic Weight (SW) - a measure of neural path strength. Grows with each correct answer and decays over time due to forgetting: the better the deck's cards are learned (the longer their review intervals), the slower the decay.
microcards.mastery_tooltip_engram: Engram - a physical memory trace. Level 10 ('Stable Engram') is the maximum, yet even it needs an occasional review: without one, even the strongest trace slowly fades.
microcards.mastery_tooltip_resonance: Resonance - a flow state (combo). A fast streak of correct answers temporarily multiplies SW.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_1: Level 1: Transient Trace. Short-term memory trace that decays rapidly without review.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_2: Level 2: Unstable Path. Initial synaptic gating, easily disrupted by interference.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_3: Level 3: Early Consolidation. First structural synaptic changes, trace becomes more resilient.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_4: Level 4: Formed Link. Synaptic transmission is optimized, basic recall is stable.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_5: Level 5: Active Synapse. Long-term potentiation (LTP) is locked, recall speed is high.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_6: Level 6: Resonant Engram. Neural ensemble synchronizes efficiently during recall.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_7: Level 7: Reinforced Memory. Recruitment of secondary pathways, high resistance to decay.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_8: Level 8: High Conductivity. Maximum signal propagation speed, near-instantaneous retrieval.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_9: Level 9: Consolidated Circuit. Memory is integrated into the neocortex and is independent of the hippocampus.
microcards.mastery_lvl_desc_10: Level 10: Stable Engram. The maximum level - the trace is firmly consolidated and fades very slowly, though even it needs a rare review.

main_dashboard_work_contour.title: Home: main work flow
main_dashboard_work_contour.summary: First introduction to the blocks through which the user starts learning.

work_contour.c0_body: Browse open materials from other authors, pick suitable complexes or theory, and add them to your library.
work_contour.c1_body: This is the main working section: see which complexes are already in your library, and what you can start, continue, or repeat.
work_contour.c2_body: Quick review mode using cards and pairs like "term - definition". This section is still being developed.

author_tools.c0_body: The task editor is where you create learning tasks: tests, clicks, open answers, and other formats for future complexes.
author_tools.c1_body: The complex editor assembles tasks into a full learning scenario: order, repetitions, linked theory, and publishing.
author_tools.c2_body: The theory centre helps store materials, link them to topics, and attach them to complexes as learning context.

activity_widgets.c0_body: Calendar and statistics come alive after learning activity: your daily plan, repetitions, accuracy, dynamics, and weak spots will appear here.
activity_widgets.c1_body: Quick access collects the complexes the user returns to most often: pinned, recent, and active.

complexes_library_navigation.title: Complexes: search and filtering
complexes_library_navigation.summary: First introduction to the complex library: search, filters, sorting, and the current summary.

search_and_filters.c0_body: Search helps you quickly find a complex by name, description, or a specific task inside it.
search_and_filters.c1_body: Keep only the complexes you need: authored, from catalogue, paused, or due for review. Sorting and a result summary are nearby.

complex_card_actions.c0_body: The card shows what this complex is: description, number of tasks, learning status, pause, and theory link.
complex_card_actions.c1_body: The main button starts a new run. If the complex is already paused, it returns the user to their saved session.
complex_card_actions.c2_body: Here you can pin the complex to quick access, export it, open it for editing, or remove it from the library.

complex_library_actions.c0_body: Creating opens the complex editor where tasks are assembled into a learning path with theory, order, and publishing.
complex_library_actions.c1_body: Import transfers a complex from a file. An access code adds a private catalogue publication directly to your library.

complex_editor_authoring.title: Complex editor: learning scenario
complex_editor_authoring.summary: How to assemble a complex from tasks, add theory, configure the study order, link tasks into chains, check readiness, and save.

complex_editor_core_info.c0_body: This is the scenario card: the name helps find the complex in the library, and the description explains what it teaches and when to use it.
complex_editor_core_info.c1_body: The top bar shows work status, composition readiness, publishing state, and saving of the current complex version.

complex_editor_theory_context.c0_body: A complex can inherit theory from topics, attach existing material, or create a separate text. This gives the learner context for tasks.
complex_editor_theory_context.c1_body: Choose where to take the theory from: the complex's topics, existing material, or a new text created inside the editor.
complex_editor_theory_context.c2_body: The demo shows the new-theory option: you can set a title, format text, add images, and save everything together with the complex.

complex_editor_task_selection.c0_body: This is where you build the working path. Order and composition matter: the complex should lead the learner from basics to consolidation.
complex_editor_task_selection.c1_body: In the Complexes tab you can choose an already-created complex and open it for editing.
complex_editor_task_selection.c2_body: Select tasks from your working library on the right. Search helps quickly find a module, topic, ID, or tag.
complex_editor_task_selection.c3_body: After selecting, tasks are added to the complex. The counter shows how many items will be added in one step.
complex_editor_task_selection.c4_label: Show hint about test task mode
complex_editor_task_selection.c5_body: "Together" means all test questions will appear consecutively. "Shuffled" mixes test questions among other complex tasks. If a test is in a chain, questions are forced together so the linked block stays intact.

complex_editor_chains.c0_body: A chain affects more than just the editor layout: when the complex runs, these tasks enter the queue as one block, not as separate elements.
complex_editor_chains.c1_body: The queue generator first groups the chain into a chunk, then balances the queue. So the order within the block is preserved during the session.

complex_editor_readiness_and_release.c0_body: The indicator checks whether there are enough tasks, types, and structure for a normal run. It is a quick check before saving.
complex_editor_readiness_and_release.c1_body: Publishing makes the complex available via the catalogue or a chosen access mode. The draft can continue to be edited separately.
complex_editor_readiness_and_release.c2_body: Saving locks in the current editor version: name, theory, selected tasks, order, and chains.

microcards_library_overview.title: Microcards: decks and review
microcards_library_overview.summary: Short cards for spaced repetition: where to see what is due, how a deck is built, and which study modes it has.

library_pulse.c0_body: "Due" are cards whose review time has come: the longer you put them off, the faster the material fades. "New" are cards you haven't studied yet. These numbers matter more than the total deck count.

library_find.c0_body: Search finds a deck by name, and the sort next to it brings what matters now to the top — for example, decks with review debt.
library_find.c1_body: You can create a deck from scratch or get a ready one: by an author's access code or from the catalog of learning materials.

library_deck_card.c0_body: The card shows the deck size and how many cards are due. A click opens the deck page with its study modes and the card list.

deck_mastery.c0_body: Every session earns synaptic weight (SW) and raises the deck level. Without reviews the weight slowly decays — so you can see which decks hold in memory and which need refreshing.
deck_mastery.c1_body: Runs cover the whole deck: Level 1 in a "know / don't know" format, Level 2 with typed answers. "Review" is the daily work on due and new cards, "Browse" is free flipping. Tips for the session itself appear on the first run, and later you can find them in the reference.

microcards_review_session.title: Microcards: review session
microcards_review_session.summary: How a session goes: reveal the answer, grade yourself honestly, bring back mistakes, and read the summary.

session_card.c0_body: The question is shown first. The card flips to the answer. In "reverse" decks the question and answer swap places, so it helps to know both sides.

session_reveal.c0_body: Try to recall the answer, then reveal the back side. In decks with typed answers there will be an input field here — the answer is checked automatically.

session_grade.c0_body: After answering, grade yourself honestly — this is the only grade, and the card's next review is scheduled from it. If you typed an answer and a correct one wasn't accepted, there is a "Correct anyway" button.

session_queue.c0_body: Here you see the synaptic weight (SW) you earned and your streak of correct answers in a row. The repeat icon shows missed cards — they come back within this same session until you answer them correctly.
session_queue.c1_body: The bar counts mastered cards, not cards passed in a row, so a mistake does not roll it back.

session_summary.c0_body: The summary shows first-try accuracy, the SW you earned, and your best streak. From here you can go back to the decks or run the review again.
session_summary.c1_body: Cards that came back through the mistake queue are collected separately — a hint of what to review next time.

calendar_daily_plan.title: Calendar: learning plan
calendar_daily_plan.summary: How to read the daily plan, schedule, activity, and memory health.

calendar_today_plan.c0_body: A short selection of reviews: mistakes, weak spots, and material that is due for a refresh.
calendar_today_plan.c1_body: The main complex for today. It helps avoid manually choosing what to study next.
calendar_today_plan.c2_body: The plan adapts to available minutes and does not suggest more than you can realistically complete.

calendar_rhythm.c0_body: The feed shows where repetitions are scheduled and how many learning actions are planned for the week.
calendar_rhythm.c1_body: The heat map quickly shows regularity: where the pace was kept and where gaps appeared.

calendar_memory_health.c0_body: If a complex is slipping, the calendar immediately shows what is best to refresh today.
calendar_memory_health.c1_body: See which complexes are holding strong and which should be repeated first.

statistics_learning_signals.title: Statistics: learning signals
statistics_learning_signals.summary: How to read general metrics and distinguish useful learning signals from reference numbers.

statistics_overall_metrics.c0_body: See how many tasks have been mastered and how much time has been spent on learning. This is overall progress, but it alone does not tell you what to study next.
statistics_overall_metrics.c1_body: Cards show the accuracy of short reviews, and the streak shows whether you have been studying regularly. These metrics help identify where material should be refreshed.

statistics_time_dynamics.c0_body: The chart shows which days had learning activity. Focus on regularity, not just the tallest bar.
statistics_time_dynamics.c1_body: Choose what to view: time or activity, then compare a period of 7, 30, or 90 days.

statistics_performance_and_complexes.c0_body: See which task types feel easier or harder. A low percentage suggests this format is worth more practice.
statistics_performance_and_complexes.c1_body: View recent complex completions. This makes it easier to see what has been reinforced and what deserves a revisit.

catalog_discovery_library.title: Catalogue: searching and selecting materials
catalog_discovery_library.summary: How to find a publication, sort results, evaluate details, and add suitable material to your library.

catalog_search_and_filters.c0_body: Enter a name, topic, or author. Search narrows results without changing section: handy for quickly checking whether ready material exists for the current task.
catalog_search_and_filters.c1_body: Filters separate all publications, complexes, theories, and already-saved materials. This is a first coarse pass before sorting and browsing cards.
catalog_search_and_filters.c2_body: Sorting changes the card order: newest first, alphabetically, by content type, or by volume. A nearby summary shows how many publications remain after search and filters.

catalog_card_and_detail.c0_body: The card gives a quick overview, while the detail panel shows the composition, linked materials, and helps decide whether to save the publication.
catalog_card_and_detail.c1_body: The catalogue does not start learning directly. First save the material: the complex will appear in complexes and the theory in the theory centre.

theory_center_library.title: Theory centre: library and links
theory_center_library.summary: How to find theory, check topic and complex links, and quickly open the material you need.

theory_center_find_and_filter.c0_body: The top block collects problem and useful slices: topics without theory, complexes with one theory, selections, and unlinked materials.
theory_center_find_and_filter.c1_body: Search works on topic, complex, and theory names. It is the fastest way to check whether the material you need already exists.
theory_center_find_and_filter.c2_body: Toggles change the result type: all theories, topics, complexes, unlinked materials, and theories with a title only.

theory_center_card_and_actions.c0_body: The card shows the author, catalogue publication, links to topics and complexes, and the last updated date.
theory_center_card_and_actions.c1_body: The button opens the theory: your own materials open in the editor, while other authors' theories from the catalogue open in view mode.

theory_editor_authoring.title: Theory editor: creating material
theory_editor_authoring.summary: How to select theory, format text, add images, save, and prepare material for publishing.

theory_editor_library_and_title.c0_body: Your theories are listed on the left. Quickly find material by name or ID and switch between saved theories.
theory_editor_library_and_title.c1_body: The top bar refers to the theory selected in the library: publication status, library limit, quick links, creating a new theory, and saving.

theory_editor_body_and_text_tools.c0_body: While text is selected, bold, italic, headings, lists, alignment, colour, and the add-image button are available here.
theory_editor_body_and_text_tools.c1_body: This area is where you write the main material. You can mix headings, lists, explanations, and images in the text.
theory_editor_body_and_text_tools.c2_body: After clicking, the image receives a selection frame. Changes from the toolbar now apply to it.
theory_editor_body_and_text_tools.c3_body: Here you can change the size, alignment, wrapping, rotation, and reflection of the image directly inside the material.

theory_editor_save_and_publish.c0_body: Saving updates your personal version of the theory. If there are unsaved changes, the button is clearly highlighted.
theory_editor_save_and_publish.c1_body: After saving you can manage publishing: keep the theory private, open it to everyone, or grant access by code.

test_editor_authoring.title: Test editor: questions and answers
test_editor_authoring.summary: How to build a test: add questions, write the wording, mark correct answers, configure feedback, and save.

test_editor_question_structure.c0_body: All test questions are visible on the left. The active question is open in the workspace, and an indicator shows answer readiness.
test_editor_question_structure.c1_body: A new question is added manually. Import opens a dialog to load questions from a file or text. Export immediately saves the current test task to a file without a separate dialog.
test_editor_question_structure.c2_body: Choose a source at the top: a file with questions or a text template. The active tab highlights which scenario is currently open.
test_editor_question_structure.c3_body: Shows the selected file, number of questions found, parse status, and a preview. The Choose file button starts loading.
test_editor_question_structure.c4_body: After checking, choose whether to add questions to the existing ones or replace the entire test, then confirm the import with the bottom button.

test_editor_question_body.c0_body: Write the wording here. Keep it short and check one specific fact, rule, or distinction.
test_editor_question_body.c1_body: Up to three illustrations can be attached to a question. They belong only to the current question.

test_editor_options.c0_body: Each row is a separate answer option. An option can contain text, an image, or both; the button on the right adds an image specifically to that option.
test_editor_options.c1_body: Clicking the option letter marks or unmarks it as correct. Marking multiple letters automatically makes the question a multiple-correct-answer question.
test_editor_options.c2_body: This button adds another answer option to the current question.
test_editor_options.c3_body: Task images are collected here. An already-uploaded image can be reused in other questions and options.

test_editor_inspector.c0_body: Determined automatically: one correct option — single choice; multiple — multiple choice.
test_editor_inspector.c1_body: The comment is shown after the answer and helps explain why it is correct.
test_editor_inspector.c2_body: One correct option — single choice; multiple — multiple choice.
test_editor_inspector.c3_body: The comment is shown after the answer and explains why it is correct.

test_editor_save.c0_body: The buttons work with editor history: roll back added elements or restore an undone action.
test_editor_save.c1_body: Before saving, the editor will verify that there is question text, at least two options, and at least one correct answer.
test_editor_save.c2_body: The indicator shows whether the test is saved or has unsaved edits.

open_answer_authoring.title: Open answer editor
open_answer_authoring.summary: How to build a free-answer task: question, reference answer, keywords, hint, requirements, and images.

open_answer_header_save.c0_body: The header shows which task is open and which editor you are working in.
open_answer_header_save.c1_body: The indicator shows whether the current edits are saved.
open_answer_header_save.c2_body: Before saving, the editor will check the question, reference answer, and selected keywords.

open_answer_question.c0_body: Formulate the task for a free-text answer. Write the question so that one or more required semantic features can be identified in the reference; those selected keywords will then be checked in the answer.

open_answer_reference.c0_body: This is the correct semantic answer. The editor uses it to prepare words and phrases that can then be marked as required.
open_answer_reference.c1_body: The button extracts candidates from the reference answer. Then choose which of them are truly important for checking.

open_answer_keywords_hint.c0_body: Clicking a word toggles it as required. The counter shows how many answer features are selected for checking.
open_answer_keywords_hint.c1_body: The hint is optional. It helps the user recall the direction of the answer without fully revealing the reference.

open_answer_sidebar.c0_body: You can require keyword order and set a maximum answer length. If a limit is set, an input restriction appears in the trainer.
open_answer_sidebar.c1_body: Up to three images can be attached to the open answer. They are saved with the task and help set context.

click_editor_authoring.title: Click editor
click_editor_authoring.summary: How to build a task where the user clicks to mark areas on an image.

click_header_save.c0_body: The header shows which Click task is open for editing.
click_header_save.c1_body: Click mode is used to mark areas on an image. Error mode opens a separate text-checking scenario.
click_header_save.c2_body: Before saving, the editor will check the image, wording, and number of required outlines.

click_prompt_rules.c0_body: Write the instruction for the user: exactly what to find and mark on the image.
click_prompt_rules.c1_body: The field sets how many correct areas the user must mark for the answer to count.

click_image_workspace.c0_body: The canvas holds the image on which the user will perform the click task.
click_image_workspace.c1_body: Use this button to add the task's first image or replace the current one.
click_image_workspace.c2_body: Plus and minus help zoom in to place an outline precisely.

click_drawing_tools.c0_body: Lasso builds an outline point by point; freehand drawing lets you trace a line by hand.
click_drawing_tools.c1_body: Close the current outline with the button or a double left-click. Delete the last point or cancel an unfinished markup here.

click_annotations_manage.c0_body: All areas appear here after markup. Outlines can be renamed directly in the list; the Highlight button temporarily highlights the area on the image, and Label controls the display of its name.
click_annotations_manage.c1_body: Selecting an outline on the image reveals its points; each point can be moved to fine-tune the boundary.
click_annotations_manage.c2_body: Text or images can be added if the Click task needs context.

click_difficulty_levels.c0_body: A standard complex has 3 iterations. Levels help distribute a single task across that path: from a simple step at the start to a harder one at the end.
click_difficulty_levels.c1_body: "All levels of type" keeps the task in every Click iteration. "Selected only" limits where it appears — e.g. only in early practice or only in the final check.
click_difficulty_levels.c2_body: L1: click a ready-made area. L2: choose the name of the found area. L3: outline the area and enter its name.

draw_editor_authoring.title: Draw editor
draw_editor_authoring.summary: How to build a task where the user traces areas on an image themselves.

draw_header_save.c0_body: Shows which Draw task is open for editing.
draw_header_save.c1_body: Before saving, the editor will check the image, wording, outlines, and area labels.

draw_prompt_rules.c0_body: Write what the user should trace. If a label is needed only at a specific level, specify it separately rather than as a mandatory action for all.
draw_prompt_rules.c1_body: The field sets how many correctly marked areas are needed to pass.

draw_image_workspace.c0_body: The user will trace the required areas on this canvas. The cleaner the image, the more precise the markup.
draw_image_workspace.c1_body: Use this button to add the task's base image or replace the current one.
draw_image_workspace.c2_body: Zoom in to stay precisely within the area boundary.

draw_tools.c0_body: Straight-line lasso places points along the boundary. Freehand drawing traces the outline with mouse movement.
draw_tools.c1_body: An outline can be completed, have its last point deleted, or have an unfinished drawing cancelled.

draw_regions_manage.c0_body: Every drawn outline ends up here. Names can be edited directly in the list.
draw_regions_manage.c1_body: Select an area on the image: the outline points appear and each can be moved for a more precise boundary.
draw_regions_manage.c2_body: Leave context for the author here: text or a hint image.

draw_difficulty_levels.c0_body: A standard complex has 3 iterations. For drawing, levels help choose where the task appears: in boundary practice or in the labelled check.
draw_difficulty_levels.c1_body: Keep all levels if the task suits any drawing iteration. Select specific levels if it is needed only for tracing or only for tracing with a label.
draw_difficulty_levels.c2_body: L1: trace the required area. L2: trace the area and label it.

click_editor_errors_authoring.title: Click error mode
click_editor_errors_authoring.summary: How to configure a Click task where the user finds erroneous fragments inside text.

click_errors_overview.c1_body: This scenario turns the Click editor into a task for finding errors in text.
click_errors_overview.c2_body: First, let's cover Words mode: the user finds erroneous fragments within a single text. Texts mode can be accessed after this block.

click_errors_words_workflow.c0_body: Errors are marked in the Main text. The Reference tab stores the model answer or hint fragments.
click_errors_words_workflow.c1_body: Enter the text where the user must find erroneous fragments.
click_errors_words_workflow.c2_body: Select a text fragment and click the button to save it as an error.
click_errors_words_workflow.c3_body: After marking, fragments appear here. The list shows each found error, its label, and actions to navigate or delete.

click_errors_reference.c0_body: The reference stores the model text and important fragments. It can be filled manually or copied from the main text, then key passages marked.

click_errors_rules_instruction.c0_body: You can require finding all errors or set a minimum number to pass.
click_errors_rules_instruction.c1_body: The instruction sets the task text for the user. If left empty, the editor substitutes a standard error-finding wording.

click_editor_errors_texts_authoring.title: Click Texts mode
click_editor_errors_texts_authoring.summary: How to configure a Click task where the user selects the correct text from options.

click_errors_texts_mode.c0_body: After switching to Texts, text options are created. One option is marked correct and the rest remain incorrect.
click_errors_texts_mode.c1_body: Press to add another text option.

click_errors_texts_instruction.c0_body: This instruction explains to the user how to choose the correct text. If left empty, the editor substitutes a standard wording.

sequence_editor_authoring.title: Sequence editor
sequence_editor_authoring.summary: How to build a task where elements are placed into levels and optionally ordered.

sequence_header_save.c0_body: The header shows which sequence is open for editing.
sequence_header_save.c1_body: Buttons help roll back edits or restore an undone action when working with levels and steps.
sequence_header_save.c2_body: Before saving, the editor will check the task text, levels, and at least two filled steps.

sequence_prompt.c0_body: Describe what the user should assemble: a process, stages, classification, or order of actions.

sequence_levels.c0_body: A level defines a group or stage. In the trainer, the user places elements into these levels.
sequence_levels.c1_body: The button creates another group for elements. Multiple levels are possible if the task requires classification or stages.

sequence_steps.c0_body: Each card is a separate step. The card text is saved as the element the user will place in their answer.
sequence_steps.c1_body: Buttons move steps left and right. If order within the level matters, this sequence will be checked.
sequence_steps.c2_body: Plus adds a new element to the current level. At least two filled elements are required to save.

sequence_sidebar_settings.c0_body: The answer is evaluated based on whether elements landed in the right levels and whether the enabled order was followed.
sequence_sidebar_settings.c1_body: Step order within a level and level order can each be enabled separately. A hint below immediately explains the chosen combination.

editor_dashboard_authoring.title: Task editor: work centre
editor_dashboard_authoring.summary: How modules, topics, tasks, search, import, and new-task creation are organised.

editor_dashboard_structure.c0_body: The counter shows how many personal tasks have been created. Premium has no limit.
editor_dashboard_structure.c1_body: The active topic is highlighted in the tree. New tasks go into it by default.
editor_dashboard_structure.c2_body: Tasks live inside topics, and topics inside modules. Selecting a topic changes the task list in the workspace.

editor_dashboard_author_tools.c0_body: Shows auto-saved task drafts: open or delete.

editor_dashboard_search_and_sort.c0_body: The top row shows which module and topic are open and lets you quickly go back up.
editor_dashboard_search_and_sort.c1_body: Search helps find a task, module, or file without manually browsing the whole structure.
editor_dashboard_search_and_sort.c2_body: The list can be ordered by date modified, alphabetically, or by task type.

editor_dashboard_task_grid.c0_body: Cards open created tasks for viewing or editing. The star adds the task to favourites.
editor_dashboard_task_grid.c1_body: This card starts creating a task in the selected topic.

editor_dashboard_create_task.c0_body: Before creating, choose the module, topic, and a clear name so the task goes to the right place immediately.
editor_dashboard_create_task.c1_body: The type determines which editor opens next: test, click, draw, sequence, or open answer.
editor_dashboard_create_task.c2_body: Detailed hints for specific task types do not launch automatically. They can be opened from the reference or the help button inside the chosen editor.

wl.k010: A learning system that keeps materials, practice, and progress together.
wl.k011: ACTRA helps users build a personal learning library, create tasks and theories, complete learning complexes, review material, and see progress in the calendar and statistics.
wl.k013: Collect theories, tasks, cards, and your own materials in one working environment.
wl.k015: Train through learning complexes, different task types, and material review.
wl.k017: Track results, activity calendar, and learning statistics.
wl.k019: Create tests, open answers, sequences, click tasks, and graphic formats.
wl.k021: Link theory, complexes, and practice so that learning doesn't fall apart into separate files.
wl.k023: Prepare materials for use, manage access, and return to working versions.
wl.k025: This project was born from an attempt to make learning suitable for those who need more than just reading a text and hoping it will stick on its own.
wl.k027: From a task to a complex and review.
wl.k028: In ACTRA the learning cycle starts with a task: you create materials, assemble them into a complex, launch a session, and see what needs improvement.
wl.k029: Tasks are created in the editor and linked to a topic.
wl.k030: A complex is assembled from ready-made tasks and can be private, public, or accessible by code.
wl.k031: A session proceeds by iterations, and the result shows errors and the next step.
wl.k033: Prepare tasks in the editor: type, topic, content, and save.
wl.k035: Combine ready-made tasks into a complex. Add theory if it is needed for preparation.
wl.k037: ACTRA delivers tasks by iterations and saves the session state.
wl.k039: See accepted tasks, errors, and what is worth improving before the next run.
wl.k041: Creation, session, and review in one learning scenario.
wl.k042: Several real system states: task creation, test session, iteration review, and theory preparation.
wl.k044: Image annotation, checkable areas, and task parameters in one working screen.
wl.k047: Current task, selected answer, and quick navigation between questions.
wl.k049: Attempt summary, next step, and error breakdown on one screen.
wl.k051: Material is open right in the editor: text, formatting, and save nearby.
wl.k061: Not memorising theory, but working with it.
wl.k062: ACTRA grew out of a very personal problem: there is usually not too little theoretical material, but too much. Yet re-reading, mechanical note-taking, and attempts to 'cram' text do not always turn knowledge into action.
wl.k063: The idea was not to create yet another place to store notes. The goal was to build an environment where existing material can gradually be turned into tasks and tested through practice.
wl.k064: This way theory stops being a page you need to 'finish reading to the end' and becomes material you can interact with: apply, compare, classify, find errors, and build connections.
wl.k066: How ACTRA turns material into practice
wl.k068: Theory can be broken down into tests, interactive tasks, sequences, open answers, and error-finding exercises.
wl.k070: Memorisation is built not on passive re-reading but on solving, choosing, matching, and trying again.
wl.k072: Theory, tasks, complex, attempt, and error review do not fall apart into separate files and tabs.
wl.k074: Quizlet once helped the author through active recall. ACTRA goes further: to a full-featured practice environment.
wl.k075: As your library grows, Premium removes workspace limits.
wl.k076: Premium is digital access for a chosen period. It removes the blockers of the free plan, unlocks the full Calendar and Statistics pages, and helps you avoid hitting a limit once your library has grown beyond its first learning materials.
wl.k084: The free plan is good for getting started but limits the number of your own tasks, complexes, theories and flashcard decks, plus catalog connections. Premium removes these limits so you can expand your library without stopping.
wl.k086: The full page with Daily Mix, schedule, activity, and memory health is unlocked. Widgets on the home screen remain available to everyone, but the full working view is in Premium.
wl.k088: Metrics by tasks, time, microcards, streaks, chart, task types, and learning complexes are available — not just a brief summary.
wl.k090: If Premium expires and free limits are exceeded, extra materials go into the Premium archive. You can open and delete them, but editing, launching, publishing, copying, or importing requires freeing a slot or renewing access.
wl.k092: If the source ended up in the Premium archive, the published version remains accessible. A new version from an archived source cannot be released until the material returns to active space.
wl.k094: Access is granted for 14, 30, or 90 days. If Premium is renewed before the current period ends, the new period is counted from the current access end date.
wl.k096: ACTRA Premium is a digital service: no physical goods are sold or delivered. Access is granted in the user's account after payment confirmation. A refund may be considered for a duplicate or accidental payment, a technical activation error, or another clear billing mistake.
